- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for 2–4 days.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overcorrects after mean reversion; if 3–5 consecutive days show price retracing to prior range, reduce forecast slope to match historical mean reversion speed.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; adjust forecast to match sentiment’s dominant polarity for 3–5 days before reversal.
